A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Var-JEPA/Var-T-JEPA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison despite repagination and the added Section B.3.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and SIGReg ablations, downstream classification results, uncertainty diagnostics, and Adult sensitivity experiments in Tables 1–5 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds comparisons of uncertainty estimators on SIM and MNIST in Appendix B.3 and Table 6.

M1.justification: The generative model, posterior factorization, weighted five-term objective, tabular architecture, masking procedure, and training algorithm are retained. Corrections to mathematical expressions and notation do not establish a changed implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Adult, Covertype, Electricity, Credit Card Default, Bank Marketing, corrupted MNIST, SIM, and the controlled latent-variable simulation. The new uncertainty comparison reuses existing SIM and MNIST scenarios without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix B.3/Table 6 introduces the first comparison against four post-hoc uncertainty estimators: Probe entropy, Probe MSP, MC dropout, and Deep ensemble. This substantially expands comparator coverage for the uncertainty contribution. Existing downstream comparators are retained; T-JEPA's auxiliary tokens were already documented in v1 Appendix D.4.

E3.justification: The added comparison evaluates uncertainty estimators on the same frozen Var-T-JEPA embeddings, using linear probes, 20 MC-dropout forward passes, and five independently trained ensemble MLPs. It uses the existing Spearman, ambiguity-detection AUC, and AURC diagnostics. Settings for retained experiments, including splits and hyperparameter tables, are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 extends the uncertainty diagnostics by testing how native latent scores compare with post-hoc scores for ambiguity detection and selective-prediction risk. The existing SIGReg/collapse ablations and Adult loss-weight, architecture, and optimization sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing experiments retain mean ± standard deviation over five runs and the single-run XGBoost convention. Table 6 adds point estimates, consistent with the existing Figure 3 diagnostics, without new confidence intervals or significance tests. Its dropout passes and ensemble members describe estimator computation rather than repeated-evaluation uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. New Table 6 repeats Figure 3's native-uncertainty scores and adds comparator results: native uncertainty ranks best on Spearman correlation and ambiguity-detection AUC, while the lowest reported AURC is 0.011 for Deep ensemble on SIM and 0.025 for MC dropout on MNIST, versus native values of 0.209 and 0.123.

T1.justification: Equations (9)–(10) restore outer expectations around the conditional KL terms, and Section 3.5 corrects the loss-gradient estimator's sign. Section 3.3 also explicitly distinguishes the weighted, beta-VAE-style surrogate from the exact negative ELBO recovered with unit weights. These are localized mathematical corrections; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows improvement over T-JEPA to real-world tabular benchmarks. The introduction replaces claimed consistent gains over both JEPA and raw-feature baselines with gains over JEPA and competitiveness with raw-feature baselines. The central variational interpretation and uncertainty contributions remain.

C2.justification: The introduction now explains that stop-gradient and EMA can help optimization without removing constant solutions from the objective. Section 3.3 narrows the entropy term's role from generally preventing collapse to preventing a deterministic point posterior, and qualifies the interpretation of the weighted objective as an exact ELBO.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 documents the new uncertainty-score constructions and their dropout-pass and ensemble sizes. Appendix D.2.5 makes the decoder-noise description consistent with the separate context and target variances already specified in v1 Appendix A.3. Existing hardware, training-time, and hyperparameter disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds historical positioning through Schmidhuber and Prelinger, discusses PhiNet v2, and sharpens the distinction from Huang's probabilistic JEPA through observation reconstruction. It also adds beta-VAE and uncertainty-estimator references. Publication and bibliographic updates to existing works do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the introduction, related work, objective interpretation, and experimental description. v2 standardizes notation and terminology, adds an Impact Statement and Section B.3, and swaps the training-algorithm and KL-annealing subsections. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6, corrects labels and notation in architecture diagrams, and adjusts Figure 3's title, caption, and placement. Table 1's caption no longer claims a coupling statistic absent from its columns; the coupling curve remains in Figure 2. These are localized display changes within the existing layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision through the ELBO and gradient corrections, qualifies the weighted objective, and better aligns summary performance claims with the unchanged results. Table 6 adds useful comparative uncertainty evidence, including unfavorable AURC rankings. Its point-only reporting and unspecified matching of classifier predictions for AURC limit the strength of that addition, but the overall gains in correctness and clarity are supported.
